title: Release Packaging and Reproducible Deliverables
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Release Packaging and Reproducible Deliverables.
Apply release packaging and reproducible deliverables to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to release packaging and reproducible deliverables.
Review common mistakes and risks in release packaging and reproducible deliverables.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using release packaging and reproducible deliverables principles.

understand.concept: A release artifact is a versioned, installable or deployable output built from source and declared dependencies. Reproducibility depends on pinned or bounded dependencies, supported Python versions, clean build environments and clear release metadata. Packaging quality must be checked after installation, not only from the source checkout.
understand.whyItMatters: A reproducible deliverable can be installed, tested and maintained consistently by someone other than its author.
understand.analogy: A sealed kit includes the parts list and instructions needed to assemble the same product elsewhere.
understand.analogyLimit: A successful local build does not prove that the artifact works on every supported platform or Python version.
understand.summary: Release Packaging and Reproducible Deliverables helps learners deliver and maintain reliable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Declare project metadata and supported Python versions. Build in a clean environment, inspect the artifact contents, install it into a fresh environment and run smoke tests. Record version, changelog and dependency policy. Avoid shipping secrets, caches, test data or local configuration.
